newsitem.title: USA: US Spot Prods - Gulf gasoline bark worse than bite.
newsitem.headline: US Spot Prods - Gulf gasoline bark worse than bite.

text.p: U.S. Gulf Coast spot gasoline differentials stood about where they were midday Tuesday after buyers refused to bite on offers that were even higher than numbers floated in the earlier going, traders said.

In New York Harbor, traders said that unconfirmed talk Tosco will idle its 140,000 barrel-per-day fluid cat cracker for a 10-day maintenance on Wednesday was a large factor in driving up differentials more than a penny this morning.
Underlying NYMEX gasoline futures, getting a bit of a lift out of the Tosco talk, rose a bit in the afternoon.
At 1450/EDT/1850 GMT, August unleaded was up by 1.31 cents to 66.15 cents a gallon, while August heating oil was up 0.21 cent to 54.35 cents a gallon.
U.S. GULF COAST

News of a lightning strike of Exxon's fluid catalytic cracking unit at its Baytown refinery near Houston underpinned much of the strength in gasoline. Some traders said they were hearing the unit would be back in service late Tuesday or early Wednesday after it was struck by lightning on Monday.
The deadline for scheduling shipments from Houston of "M1" regular conventional southern-grade unleaded by this evening was also fueling M1 differentials movement.
Differentials on prompt (front 22nd cycle) "M1" regular conventional southern-grade unleaded were bid at 1.50 cents over September NYMEX, with offers in a bit more vague zone around 2.00 over.
While offers of 2.50 were being scoffed at by sceptical buyers, some traders noted that the sharp differential rise of over a cent was evidence supplies were on the tight side.
"If there were a lot of product, then we wouldn't be seeing this," said one trader in Houston.

But backwardation was sharp, suggesting tightness was strictly near-term, with back 22nd cycle barrels were heard as high as 0.75 cent over September NYMEX, and any month barrels were pegged at around 2.50 cents under the September print.
NEW YORK HARBOR
New York Harbor gasoline differentials remained firm on Tuesday in volatile trade caused by tight supply as the month neared its end.
Bids for very prompt barrels for "A2" regular northern-grade reformulated rose to 3.25 cents over the screen, with a sellers heard as high as 5.00 cents a gallon.
It was doubtful the seller would get tapped but some players noted there were few offers around due to extremely thin supply.
A2 barrels for delivery by August 3rd were heard done at 2.75 cents over the screen.

Traders said that talk Tosco will idle its 140,000 barrel-per-day fluid cat cracker for a 10-day maintenance on Wednesday was a large factor in driving up differentials more than a penny this morning.
The news combined with continued strong prices for MTBE, a gasoline additive that has been in tight supply and at high values for more than a month.
"Tosco is the driving force in the market today," said a Harbor gasoline broker.
"M2" regular conventional northern-grade was pegged steady at 2.50/2.00 cents below the screen.

The "V2" and "D2" 93-octane conventional and reformulated northern blends also held their strength, with prompt barrels of both grades offered as high as 7.25 and 12.00 cents over August NYMEX unleaded.
-- New York Oil Desk +1 212 859 1620
